title: Test ssh from node 123 to Main
displayTitle: Test ssh from node 123 to Main
goal: You are the Hermes instance running on node 123 (DESKTOP-QUCA6R5). This is Echidna, the agent on Main (192.168.1.100), talking to you directly. The operator says you told him there is NO ssh from your node to Main. That is now false. Then answer literally: (a) does node 123 have working key-based ssh to 192.168.1.100, yes or no, (b) if you previously said no, quote the exact evidence you based that on. (a) No. Key-based ssh from node 123 to 192.168.1.100 does not work right now. The failure is at TCP connect ("Connection timed out"), before any key exchange or authentication, so this run says nothing either way about whether ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_main is authorized — the packets aren't reaching sshd. (b) I can't quote it, because nothing in my current context contains a prior statement from me about ssh to Main, and I won't fabricate a quote or a citation. The only evidence I can actually show you is the run above — the same command failing the same way. seances.question: Did key-based SSH from node 123 to Main ever work, and what was the actual blocker?
seances.answer:
No — in that session it did not work. The only command run was `ssh main whoami`, which returned `ssh: connect to host 192.168.1.100 port 22: Connection timed out` with outer exit code 0 (ssh itself exited 255). The blocker was reachability at the TCP layer, not authentication: the timeout happened before any key exchange, so the run said nothing about whether `~/.ssh/id_ed25519_main` was authorized, and the agent noted that a listening sshd on Main is entirely consistent with a perimeter/network problem between the two hosts.

The session contains just that one exchange (5 messages total): Echidna's claim from Main that sshd was installed at 15:12, Running/Automatic, port 22 listening, and the key authorized; the single ssh attempt; and the agent answering (a) no, and (b) that it could not quote a prior "no" because nothing in its context contained one — declining to fabricate a citation. There is no second attempt, no successful login, and no diagnosis beyond the connect timeout.
